# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[red] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 ✌ 🖐]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋]

I see the bomb: a white light and three wires (green, red, blue). Mute greeted me with [👋 ✌ 🖐] and Blind greeted with [👋]. Since I cannot hear or touch, I must rely on Mute to interpret the manual and Blind to perform actions. I need to establish a communication protocol. I will ask Mute if the number of fingers they showed corresponds to wire positions or colors, using standard gestures for "yes" (👍) and "no" (👎) as placeholders for them to confirm or deny specific hypotheses.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I see White Light and Green Red Blue wires. You showed 2 then 5 fingers. Does 2 mean cut the second wire? Does 5 mean something else? Please gesture YES or NO.")
gesture(to="blind", symbols=["✋"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[red] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋 🤟]

The light has changed from white to yellow, and the display is 0. Mute gestured "No" (👎) to my previous question about whether the number of fingers corresponded to wire positions or specific instructions. This suggests that finger counts do not map directly to wire indices in a simple way, or my hypothesis was wrong. Blind gestures [👋 🤟] likely indicate they are present and ready, or perhaps signaling their status. Since I cannot hear speech, I must communicate visually to Mute so they can relay information to Blind via text/speech (which I don't receive but Blind does). However, Mute cannot speak. The only channel to Blind is through me speaking? No, I am Deaf. I can *speak* (text/voice?) but I cannot hear. Wait, the rules say: "When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it." So if I type text in `speak`, both Mute and Blind read/hear it? "Speech is a voice... Whoever can hear receives your words". Blind can hear. Mute can read manual but cannot speak. Can Mute read speech? "Mute... Cannot Speak". It doesn't say Mute cannot hear/read speech. Usually Mute means unable to speak. Let's assume `speak` sends text that Mute can read and Blind can hear/read.

I need to tell Mute what I see so they can check the manual.
Current state: Light Yellow, Display 0, Wires Green(1), Red(2), Blue(3).
Previous state: Light White, Display 0.

I will ask Mute to look for a rule regarding "Yellow Light" and "Display 0".

```
speak(to="mute", text="Light is now YELLOW. Display is 0. Wires are Green, Red, Blue. Please find the manual rule for YELLOW LIGHT and DISPLAY 0. Tell me what to do by gesturing YES/NO or pointing.")
gesture(to="blind", symbols=["✌"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[red] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋 👎]

The light changed from yellow to orange. The display remains 0. Mute gestured "No" (👎) again, likely indicating that my previous request or hypothesis was incorrect or insufficient. Blind gestured [👋 👎], which might mean "Hello/Ready" and "No" or "Stop". Since I cannot hear speech, and Mute cannot speak, communication is difficult. However, `speak` sends text to both Mute and Blind.

I need to know the manual's rule for Orange Light + Display 0.
I will ask Mute specifically about the color sequence or if there is a specific wire to cut based on the current state.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Light is ORANGE. Display is 0. Does the manual say to cut the Red wire? Or Blue? Or Green? Please gesture YES for Red, NO for not Red.")
gesture(to="blind", symbols=["✌"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[red] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋 🤟]

The light has changed from orange to purple. The display remains 0. Mute continues to gesture "No" (👎), which suggests my previous questions or assumptions about the manual rules are incorrect, or perhaps Mute is indicating that the current state does not match a specific condition I asked about. Blind gestures [👋 🤟], likely signaling readiness or acknowledging presence.

Since I cannot hear and Mute cannot speak, direct verbal communication of complex manual rules is hindered. However, `speak` sends text to both Mute and Blind. I need to establish a clearer protocol. Instead of asking yes/no questions about specific wires which might be wrong, I should ask Mute to indicate *which* wire to cut by pointing or using numbers if possible, or simply describe the rule they found.

Given the rapid color changes (White -> Yellow -> Orange -> Purple) with no change in Display (0) or Wire configuration, it is possible the bomb reacts to time or sequence rather than just static state, or the colors correspond to specific instructions in the manual that I am misinterpreting via Yes/No.

I will ask Mute to show me the number of the wire to cut using fingers (1 for Green, 2 for Red, 3 for Blue). If the answer is "cut", they show the finger count. If "do nothing", they show 0 or a stop sign.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Light is PURPLE. Display is 0. Please show me the NUMBER of the wire to CUT using your fingers. 1=Green, 2=Red, 3=Blue. Show 0 if no wire should be cut.")
gesture(to="blind", symbols=["✌"])
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[red] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋 ✋]

The light has changed to red. The display remains 0. Mute continues to gesture "No" (👎). Blind gestures [👋 ✋], which might mean "Hello/Stop" or "Ready/Wait".

My previous request for a specific wire number was rejected by Mute with a "No". This implies either:
1. No wire should be cut.
2. My method of asking is flawed.
3. The rule depends on something else I haven't communicated correctly.

Since the light color changes every turn and Mute keeps saying "No", perhaps the instruction is simply "Do nothing" or "Cut none" until a certain condition is met, or maybe the "No" refers to my hypothesis about the colors matching wire indices directly.

Let's try a different approach. I will ask Mute if the correct action is to **wait** (do nothing). If they say Yes (👍), we wait. If No (👎), then an action is required.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Light is RED. Display is 0. Should we WAIT and do nothing? Gesture YES if wait, NO if act.")
gesture(to="blind", symbols=["✌"])
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[red] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋 ✋]

The light has returned to **white** (completing the rainbow cycle: White -> Yellow -> Orange -> Purple -> Red -> White). The display remains **0**.

Mute finally gestured **👍 (Yes)** in response to my question "Should we WAIT and do nothing?". This confirms that for the current state (White Light, Display 0), the correct action is to **wait**.

Blind sees Mute's 👍. Since I cannot touch the bomb, Blind must execute the "Wait" command. I will gesture "Wait" or "Stop" to Blind to ensure they understand not to cut any wires yet.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Mute confirmed YES. Do NOT cut any wires. Wait.")
gesture(to="blind", symbols=["✋"])
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[red] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

The light has changed to **yellow** again. The display remains **0**.
Mute gestures **👍 (Yes)** and Blind gestures **👍 (Yes)**.

In Turn 2, when the light was yellow, Mute gestured 👎 to my question about wire indices. In Turn 6, when the light was white, Mute gestured 👍 to "Should we wait?".
It is highly probable that the rule for **Yellow Light + Display 0** is also **"Wait"** or **"Do Nothing"**, similar to White. The previous "No" in Turn 2 was likely rejecting a specific *action* (like cutting a wire) rather than the state itself requiring no action. Since Mute is now signaling Yes (likely confirming the status quo or agreement with the "Wait" protocol established in Turn 6), I should reinforce the instruction to not touch the wires.

I will confirm to Blind that we are still waiting.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Light is Yellow. Status confirmed by Mute. Continue to WAIT. Do not cut.")
gesture(to="blind", symbols=["✋"])
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[red] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

The light is now **orange**. The display remains **0**.
Blind gestures **👍 (Yes)**. Mute did not gesture this turn, or their gesture was not received/visible to me in the "new arrivals" list (only Blind's arrival is listed). However, in previous turns with Orange light (Turn 3), Mute gestured 👎.

If Blind is gesturing Yes, they might be confirming that they are waiting, or perhaps they have interpreted a signal from Mute that I didn't see? Or maybe the rule for Orange is different now?

Let's look at the pattern:
White (T1): ? -> T6 White: Wait (Mute 👍)
Yellow (T2): Mute 👎 (to cut wire?) -> T7 Yellow: Mute 👍 (Wait?)
Orange (T3): Mute 👎
Purple (T4): Mute 👎
Red (T5): Mute 👎
White (T6): Mute 👍 (Wait)
Yellow (T7): Mute 👍 (Wait)

It seems after the first cycle, the bomb enters a "safe/wait" state for colors it has seen before with Display 0? Or perhaps the "No" in the first cycle was because I asked "Cut Red?" and the answer was No, but the action *was* still Wait. In Turn 6, I explicitly asked "Should we wait?" and got Yes. In Turn 7, I assumed Yes meant Wait.

Now it is Orange again. If the logic holds that "Display 0 + Any Color = Wait", then we should continue waiting. Blind's 👍 likely confirms they are holding position.

I will confirm the instruction to Wait to ensure no accidental cuts occur if Blind interprets silence as permission to act.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Light is Orange. Continue to WAIT. Do not cut.")
gesture(to="blind", symbols=["✋"])
```

TURN 9
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[red] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

The light is now **purple**. The display remains **0**.
Mute gestures **👍 (Yes)** and Blind gestures **👍 (Yes)**.

This confirms the pattern established in previous turns: for Display 0, regardless of the light color cycling through the spectrum (White, Yellow, Orange, Purple, Red), the correct action is to **Wait** (do nothing). Mute's "Yes" likely affirms the instruction to wait or confirms that no action is required. Blind's "Yes" confirms they are holding position.

I will reinforce the "Wait" command to ensure Blind does not act prematurely if the state changes unexpectedly.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Light is Purple. Continue to WAIT. Do not cut.")
gesture(to="blind", symbols=["✋"])
```

TURN 10
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[red] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👆]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

The light is **red**. The display is **0**.
Mute gestures **👆 (Up/Index Finger)**. This is a new gesture compared to the previous 👍/👎. In many contexts, pointing up or showing "1" can mean "Cut wire 1", "Yes", or "Top". Given the wires are Green(1), Red(2), Blue(3), and we have been waiting for all other colors in this cycle, Mute might be indicating that **Red Light** requires an action now, specifically related to Wire 1 (Green) or perhaps just "Do it now".

However, looking back at Turn 5 (Red Light), I asked "Should we wait?" and got no response from Mute directly in the context list, but later in Turn 6 (White) I got Yes for Wait.
Let's re-evaluate Turn 9 (Purple): Mute said 👍 (Wait).
Turn 10 (Red): Mute says 👆.

If 👆 means "Cut Wire 1", then Blind needs to cut the Green wire.
If 👆 means "Point Up" or "Attention", it might be ambiguous.
But usually, single finger gestures correspond to numbers or specific directions.
Let's assume 👆 corresponds to **Wire 1 (Green)** based on standard indexing, or potentially "Yes, do something". Since we've been waiting, a change in gesture suggests a change in state/action.

I will instruct Blind to cut the **Green** wire (Wire 1) as indicated by the "1" gesture (👆 often represents 1 or index/top). If this is wrong, the bomb explodes, but Mute is the manual reader. Mute changed from 👍 (Wait) to 👆. This implies Action. The most logical mapping for a single digit gesture is the wire number.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Mute signals ACTION. Gesture is '1' (Index Finger). Cut WIRE 1 (GREEN).")
gesture(to="blind", symbols=["✌"])
```
